evidence_label: ICE SEVP 2023 Top 500 F-1 Schools active-record table

Treat the 0-to-4,616 IPEDS movement as a confirmed reporting/scope discontinuity for bounded discussion while retaining the official IPEDS series in aggregate calculations.

evidence_label: Collin College FY2025 ACFR Fall Student Profile

evidence_label: Florida Department of Education 2024 and 2025 Florida College System Fact Books

evidence_label: Trine University fall 2024 record-enrollment announcement

evidence_label: Campbellsville University institutional enrollment reports
analyst_note: IPEDS declines from 4,408 U.S. nonresident students in fall 2023 to 3,050 in fall 2024. institution: The University of Texas at Dallas
evidence_label: University of Texas System FY 2026 Operating Budget Summary
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 6,828 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 5,603 in Fall 2024, a decline of 1,225. That decline is concentrated at the graduate level: graduate nonresidents fall from 5,883 to 4,398 (-1,485), while undergraduate nonresidents rise from 945 to 1,205 (+260). The University of Texas System's official FY 2026 Operating Budget Summary independently reports that UT Dallas Fall 2024 enrollment declined 3.3%, from 30,885 to 29,886 students, exactly matching the project IPEDS all-student endpoints, and states that the decline was largely attributed to normalization of international master's enrollment after a post-pandemic surge, together with graduation of unusually large delayed cohorts. UT Dallas's 2024-25 Common Data Set also reports 1,205 undergraduate nonresidents, exactly matching the project Fall 2024 undergraduate component. These official sources independently support the direction and graduate/international concentration of the decline, but they do not publish a like-for-like all-student Fall 2024 international/nonresident headcount or establish definition identity with IPEDS. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority and clear only bounded direction- and graduate-concentration discussion; do not substitute an institutional count or quantify causation beyond the institution's own statement.

evidence_label: St. Francis College institutional census archive
analyst_note: IPEDS rises from 1,791 to 3,011 U.S. nonresident students, almost entirely at the graduate level. St. Francis College's official Fall 2023 census reports 242 undergraduate and 1,549 graduate international students, summing exactly to 1,791; its Fall 2024 census reports 221 undergraduate and 2,768 graduate international students, summing to 2,989, within 22 students of the IPEDS total and matching the sharp graduate-driven increase. The institutional label is not assumed definition-identical to IPEDS, so this independently corroborates level and direction for bounded discussion while IPEDS remains the numerical authority.

evidence_label: CCRI Institutional Effectiveness dashboard and F-1 international-student definition
analyst_note: IPEDS jumps from 12 to 1,188 U.S. nonresident students between Fall 2023 and Fall 2024. CCRI's official Institutional Effectiveness enrollment dashboard independently reports total enrollment of 12,518 in Fall 2023 and 12,275 in Fall 2024, exactly matching the project IPEDS totals for both years. CCRI's official international-student admissions page separately defines an international student as a foreign national studying on an F-1 non-immigrant temporary visa and explicitly excludes U.S. citizens, permanent residents, eligible non-immigrant visa holders, refugees, asylees, and temporary protected status populations. That F-1-only admissions construct is narrower than the project IPEDS U.S. nonresident category, and the enrollment dashboard does not expose a directly comparable nonresident-status series. The exact all-student totals therefore corroborate the institutional frame while the explicit visa definition explains why CCRI's public international-student surface cannot validate the 12-to-1,188 nonresident jump. Preserve IPEDS in aggregates and keep institution-specific interpretation held pending a directly comparable residency/citizenship measure.

evidence_label: University of North Texas Fall fact-sheet archive

evidence_label: ICE SEVP 2024 Top 500 F-1 Schools active-record table
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports zero U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 930 in Fall 2024, with all 930 latest-year nonresidents in the graduate population; total enrollment rises from 1,037 to 1,145. It nevertheless independently corroborates a material upward international-student direction into 2024 and a large latest-year international presence, so clear only bounded direction-level discussion while IPEDS remains the numerical authority.

analyst_note: IPEDS falls from 192 U.S. nonresident students in 2023 to zero in 2024 while the source-status flag changes from reported (R) to zero (Z). evidence_label: CSU Global 2024 Annual Data Book and international admissions definition
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series rises from 130 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 to 313 in Fall 2024, an increase of 183. CSU Global's official international-student admissions page says students can earn a U.S. degree from their home country because the university is 100% online; it defines international applicants by prior education outside the United States or non-native English status and explicitly states that CSU Global is not SEVP-certified and does not issue or recertify student visas. The university's official 2024 Annual Data Book separately reports 14,857 students served across the 2022-23 academic year and says CSU Global serves students in all 50 states, six U.S. territories, and 52 countries. Those institution-defined international and academic-year populations intentionally include remote global learners and are not a Fall-census visa/residency measure comparable to IPEDS U.S. nonresident status. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority and keep the +183 institution-specific movement held; do not infer an IPEDS nonresident count from CSU Global's international-applicant, country-of-study, or academic-year service metrics.

evidence_label: WSCUC June 2025 CIAM accreditation team report
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 163 total students and 159 U.S. nonresidents in Fall 2023, then 344 total students and 338 U.S. nonresidents in Fall 2024, an increase of 179 nonresidents. WSCUC's official June 2025 accreditation team report independently states that CIAM enrollment grew from 163 in Fall 2023 to 346 in Fall 2024, exactly matching the project 2023 total and landing only two students above the project 2024 total. The same report says 97.5% of Fall 2023 students identified as U.S. Non-Residents, which on the reported 163-student total implies about 159 and reproduces the project baseline after rounding, but says only 24.6% identified as U.S. Non-Residents in Fall 2024, implying about 85 of 346 rather than the project IPEDS endpoint of 338. WSCUC also notes that more disaggregated country-of-origin, visa-status, and state-residency data would be useful for understanding CIAM's student population. The institutional percentages are rounded and are not substituted for the official IPEDS counts. The near-identical total-enrollment frame together with the sharply different latest-year U.S. Non-Resident composition establishes a reporting/classification discontinuity, so preserve IPEDS in aggregate calculations and clear only bounded discussion that the +179 movement is not independently confirmed as substantive nonresident growth.

evidence_label: Anderson University Center for Global Engagement and 2024 International Graduate School evidence
analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports zero U.S. nonresident students in 2022, 176 in Fall 2023, and zero again in Fall 2024, with all three values marked reported; total enrollment rises from 4,325 to 4,710 between the two latest fall endpoints. Anderson University's December 11, 2024 announcement documents 27 initial International Graduate School graduates across the Summer and Fall terms, including 20 Fall graduates, primarily from India with students from Spain and France, and states that the school had offered classes since January 2023. Its August 21, 2024 enrollment announcement says the International Graduate School was being launched for the 2024-25 year with master's programs offered to international students, and the current Center for Global Engagement reports more than 400 international students enrolled from more than 38 countries. The later 400-plus figure is not used as a Fall 2024 replacement count, and the institution-defined international population is not assumed definition-identical to IPEDS U.S. nonresident status. Taken together, the same-year program and graduate evidence plus later continuity make a literal disappearance interpretation of the reported 2024 zero untenable, but they do not establish a like-for-like 2024 EFNRALT endpoint or corroborate the -176 movement as a substantive enrollment decline. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority, do not substitute any institutional count, and clear only bounded reporting-discontinuity discussion.

evidence_label: Reformed University accreditation and authorization
analyst_note: Reformed University reports 130 U.S. nonresident students in 2023 and then leaves the project's 2024 analytic universe. The official IPEDS directory record remains active and degree-granting in 2024 (`CYACTIVE=1`, `DEGGRANT=1`) but changes `PSET4FLG` from 1 to 2, which places it outside the project's First Look/Digest universe rule. Reformed University's current accreditation page independently confirms that the institution remains active and authorized to enroll international students. The exit is therefore a confirmed analytic-classification change, not a campus closure.

evidence_label: New York State Education Department closure record
analyst_note: The institution leaves the 2024 analytic universe after reporting 115 U.S. nonresident students in 2023. New York State Education Department records The College of Saint Rose as closed on December 31, 2024, with academic instruction ending earlier in 2024. The universe exit is therefore an expected structural event rather than an unexplained data disappearance.
